chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who said to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be whipped.' I said, 'So if he were to repeat it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be whipped, for he would probably stop.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a husband who claims his wife was not a virgin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal consequence for a husband who falsely accuses his wife of pre-marital sexual inexperience (ghayr ṣāḥibah), prescribing corporal punishment to deter the claim. The Imam’s statement that he 'will soon cease' highlights the pedagogical and corrective nature of the punishment in Shia jurisprudence, aiming to resolve the dispute through repeated accountability rather than immediate divorce or annulment. This ruling is often discussed in the context of ḥudūd al-zinā and taʿzīr, emphasizing the husband's burden of proof or the presumption of virginity unless proven otherwise.
